claims.content: To report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.

goal.raw_text: To report the existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.

claims.content: System Operator
An emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts exists.
For reporting on a previously reported emergency point, reporting is performed through operator action only.
If a JU is reporting on a previously reported emergency point, that JU has additional or more current information on the point.

If another JU is to assume R^2 for an emergency point, one of the following has occurred: a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received on the emergency point, the unit with R^2 is declared inactive, or no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals.
The emergency is not on a reference point or space/ballistic missile track.
An emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts is to be reported by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.

trigger.raw_text: An emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts is to be reported by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.

claims.content: System Operator initiates reporting of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.
Assign a TN(s) to the emergency point reported on the interface by the reporting JU.

If the emergency point is related to a previously reported track/point, include the TN, Previously Reported associated with the emergency point as amplifying information, and use a TN, Reference different from the TN, Previously Reported.

When available, include IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) in the J3.1 message; the IFF/SIF data shall contain the IFF/SIF modes and codes of the previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated.
For reporting on a previously reported emergency point, perform the report through operator action only when the JU has additional or more current information on the point.
When assuming R^2 for an emergency point, use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
1. If the emergency point is not related to a previously reported track/point, the J3.1 message does not require the TN, Previously Reported as amplifying information.
2. If the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.
3. If IFF/SIF data are not available, the condition for transmitting IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) in the J3.1 message is not met.
4. If the JU does not have additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point, the condition for reporting on that point through operator action only is not met.
5. If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received on the emergency point, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R^2 for the point.
6. If the unit with R^2 is declared inactive, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R^2 for the point.
7. If no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R^2 for the point.
8. When a JU assumes R^2 for an emergency point, it shall use the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
If the emergency condition is on a reference point or space/ballistic missile track, the emergency shall not be initiated; exit the use case without initiating an emergency point report.

If the reporting JU is reporting on a previously reported emergency point but does not have additional or more current information on the point, it may not perform the report through operator action only; exit the use case without reporting on that emergency point.

If a J3.1 emergency point related to a previously reported track/point would have a TN, Reference that is not different from the TN, Previously Reported, the message does not satisfy the requirement; exit the use case without transmitting the noncompliant J3.1 message.
If an alert is being considered for the J3.1 Emergency Point message, alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message because these points cannot be filtered; exit the alert path.
The existence of an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts has been reported by transmitting an emergency point as a J3.1 message.
The emergency point reported on the interface has been assigned a TN(s) by the reporting JU.

If the emergency point is related to a previously reported track/point, the J3.1 message contains, as amplifying information, the TN, Previously Reported associated with the emergency point, and the emergency point has a TN, Reference different from the TN, Previously Reported.

When available, IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) are transmitted in the J3.1 message, and the IFF/SIF data in the J3.1 message contain the IFF/SIF modes and codes of the previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated.
The latest JU to report the emergency point has R^2 for that point.
If a JU assumes R^2 for an emergency point, it uses the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
If the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 message, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.
No alert is used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message because these points cannot be filtered.
